Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=3y,\,y(0)=1
$$

Suppose we wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={e}^{3x},$ compute the local truncation error ${τ}_{1}$ for the first step starting at $x=0$ with step size $Δx=0.2.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2x+1,\,y(0)=0
$$

Suppose we wish to approximate the solution using the following numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{6}(x+{y}^{′})\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{2}+x,$ compute the local truncation error, ${τ}_{6},$ for the step starting at $x=1$ with step size $Δx=0.2.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.

${τ}_{6}≈$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{2}+x.$ So, the $y$-value at the start of the step $x=1$ is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(1)=2.$ Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at the start of the step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(1) & =2(1)+1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment at this step is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{6}(x+{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(1))\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(1+3)\cdot 0.2 \\  & ≈0.1333.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1+0.2) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1.2) \\  & =(1.2)^{2}+1.2 \\  & =2.64\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for the step starting at $x=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{6} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1.2)-({y}_{\text{exact}}(1)+Δy) \\  & =2.64-(2+0.1333) \\  & ≈0.507\end{aligned}
$$
